rules.title: Philadelphia ban on algorithmic rent coordination
rules.requirement: Restricts landlords' use of algorithmic rent-coordination or revenue-management services. Tenant suits allege subscription to and use of RealPage services violates the ordinance. An aggrieved person may elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, plus equitable relief, interest, and attorney fees and costs.
rules.key_value: $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, plus fees and costs

coverage.summary: The secondary source states no building, unit-count or landlord-size coverage limits.

rules.effective_date_note: The only source, a law-firm alert, gives the month only ('effective February 2025'). No exact day is available. Status in_force is inferred because February 2025 is before the query date of 2026-10-01.
rules.quoted_span: Philadelphia’s ordinance permits an aggrieved person to elect statutory damages of $2,000 per violation or treble actual damages, together with equitable relief, interest and attorney fees and costs.
rules.review_note: This record rests only on a secondary source (Morgan Lewis alert, Aug. 21, 2026). The ordinance text is not captured, so these points still need verification against the official Phila. Code § 9-813: the prohibited conduct, the definitions of covered software, the exact effective date and any exemptions. The alert also notes that many local ordinances may face challenges to municipal authority.
rules.source_notes: The alert reports the ordinance is at issue in Liu v. Willow Bridge Property Co. and RealPage Inc. (Phila. C.P.) and in Jahanbakhsh v. Greystar.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Private remedies include treble actual damages or $2,000 per violation
